questions.stem: Steel is mainly an alloy of which two elements?
questions.explanation: Steel is iron with a small, controlled amount of carbon.

questions.stem: Increasing the carbon content of a plain steel generally makes it:
options: Harder and stronger but less ductile
questions.explanation: More carbon raises hardness and strength but reduces ductility and weldability.

questions.stem: Brass is an alloy made mainly of:
questions.explanation: Brass is copper and zinc. Bronze is copper and tin.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes a non-ferrous metal?
options: A metal that is always magnetic
Any metal used below the waterline
A metal that contains no significant iron
questions.explanation: Non-ferrous metals (copper, aluminium, zinc, brass, bronze) are not iron-based.

questions.stem: The flash point of a fuel is the:
options: Lowest temperature at which it gives off enough vapour to ignite briefly when a flame is present
Temperature at which it burns without any ignition source
questions.explanation: A low flash point means vapour can ignite at ordinary temperatures.

questions.stem: Diesel is preferred to gasoline aboard vessels mainly because diesel:
options: Has a higher flash point and gives off less explosive vapour
questions.explanation: Higher flash point makes diesel much safer to store and handle on a vessel.

questions.stem: Oily rags left in a pile in a warm space are dangerous because they can:
options: Heat up and ignite on their own
questions.explanation: Oxidising oil generates heat that can lead to spontaneous combustion. Store rags in a closed metal container.

questions.stem: Which fire class involves flammable liquids such as fuel and oil?
questions.explanation: A is ordinary combustibles, B is flammable liquids, C is live electrical equipment.

questions.stem: Fuel tank vent outlets are fitted with fine wire mesh mainly to:
options: Keep dirt out of the fuel
Stop flame from entering the tank
questions.explanation: The mesh acts as a flame arrester.

questions.stem: Quick-closing valves on fuel tanks let the crew:
options: Increase fuel flow to the engine
Shut off fuel supply from a position outside the machinery space
Drain water from the tank bottom
questions.explanation: In an engine-room fire you must be able to stop fuel without entering the space.

questions.stem: An alarm that sounds before a fixed engine-room smothering system discharges is there to:
options: Warn people to leave and make sure everyone is accounted for
questions.explanation: The gas is dangerous to people, so the space must be evacuated and closed first.

questions.stem: Compared with a weathertight door, a watertight door is built to:
options: Prevent the spread of fire only
Keep out water under pressure when compartments flood
questions.explanation: Watertight doors maintain subdivision. Weathertight doors only keep out weather and spray.

questions.stem: Which machinery is normally stoppable from outside the engine room?
options: Main engines, fuel supply and ventilation fans
questions.explanation: Emergency stops outside the space let you shut down fuel and air feeding a fire.

questions.stem: Before servicing a machine that could start automatically, the most important step is to:
options: Run it for an hour first
Isolate it and lock out the power so it cannot start
questions.explanation: Lockout and tag-out protects you from accidental start-up.

questions.stem: WHMIS helps engine-room workers by providing:
options: Labels and safety data sheets for hazardous products
questions.explanation: WHMIS is hazard communication for workplace chemicals.

questions.stem: Which set lists the three basic workers' rights under occupational health and safety law in Canada?
options: Right to overtime, right to a pension, right to strike
Right to a cabin, right to leave, right to a bonus
Right to know, right to participate, right to refuse unsafe work
Right to inspect, right to fine, right to hire
questions.explanation: Know, participate, refuse. Check provincial and federal wording with an examiner.

questions.stem: Before entering a confined space such as a tank, you must at minimum:
options: Hold your breath and enter quickly
Test the atmosphere and make sure it is safe and ventilated, with a standby person
Enter if the hatch has been open for a minute
Send in a lit torch to check for gas
questions.explanation: Oxygen deficiency and toxic or flammable gas kill quickly. Test, ventilate, control entry.

questions.stem: Hot work (welding, grinding, cutting) aboard should only start after:
options: The engine has been running for 10 minutes
Surrounding hazards are cleared and a fire watch and extinguisher are in place
questions.explanation: Remove combustibles, check adjoining spaces, and keep a fire watch.

questions.stem: An oil record book is used to:
options: Record oil transfers, bunkering and bilge discharges as required by regulation
questions.explanation: It documents the vessel's handling of oil and oily mixtures.

questions.stem: During bunkering, the most important thing to establish first is:
options: Reliable communication between the vessel and the fuel source
questions.explanation: If something goes wrong you must be able to stop the transfer instantly.

questions.stem: A Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP) is mainly used:
options: As a guide for responding to an oil spill
questions.explanation: It lists who to call and what to do to stop and contain a spill.

questions.stem: If your vessel causes or may have caused pollution you should:
options: Record it only in the log
Report it immediately to the Coast Guard
questions.explanation: Report promptly to the Coast Guard through MCTS, then follow your emergency plan.

questions.stem: The engine-room log is used to:
options: Record machinery readings, events and maintenance
questions.explanation: It documents operation and supports reporting if something goes wrong.

questions.stem: If the main engine stops unexpectedly you should first:
options: Inform the master and investigate the cause before attempting a restart
questions.explanation: Tell the bridge, check for obvious causes, and restart only if safe.

questions.stem: If a bump suggests the vessel has grounded, the engine-room operator should:
options: Report to the master and check bilges, shaft and stern gland for damage
questions.explanation: Grounding can open the hull or damage the propeller and shaft.

questions.stem: In an engine-room fire the usual order is:
options: Add fuel to starve the fire
Raise the alarm, stop fuel and ventilation, evacuate and then use the fixed system if needed
Continue working until the smoke thickens
questions.explanation: Isolate fuel and air, account for everyone, then discharge the fixed system on orders.

questions.stem: On hearing the alarm that warns of fire-extinguishing gas discharge you should:
questions.explanation: The gas can displace breathable air, and the alarm is your only warning.

questions.stem: A Small Vessel Machinery Operator - Restricted certificate is valid:
options: Only on the specified passenger vessel named on it, under 750 kW
questions.explanation: The SVMO-R is vessel-specific.
